title: Images and files offline, and the disk that fills up

videos.script:
A session is a few bytes. The notes for a course can be thirty megabytes, and a file that size changes the rules. {{blob}} It does not go in the database. It goes on the disk, and the database keeps a row that says where.

That row makes a promise: the file is whole, and it is there. Today you keep that promise in three bad moments. {{tunnel}} When the network stops halfway, and the download has to pick up where it stopped. {{full}} When the disk runs out, and a half file must not look like a whole one. {{sweep}} And when, despite all that, a file and its row drift apart.

You will fill a disk on purpose. Linux has a device that is always full, and writing to it gives exactly the error a full phone gives.
